title: Taking away by hopping back on a number line
examples: How do I take away on a number line?
Which way do I hop to take away?

explain.say: Imagine you have twelve sweets and you eat five. How many are left? Let us find out by hopping backwards on the number line. Look at the board.

draw.text: Taking away by hopping back on a number line

explain.say: First, find twelve and put your finger on it. That is how many you start with. Taking away means going back, towards the smaller numbers. Which way is back?
Now hop back five times: eleven, ten, nine, eight, seven. Hold up a finger for each hop. Five hops back, and you land on seven. Twelve take away five is seven!
Try ten take away three. Start at ten, and hop back three: nine, eight, seven. Seven again! Can you do the hops with your finger?
Big hops can help too. Twenty take away ten: one giant hop back of ten lands on ten. Super hopping! Challenge: what is fifteen take away five?

faq.q: How do I take away on a number line?
faq.a: Find the starting number, then hop back one space for each number you take away. Where you land is the answer.

faq.q: Which way do I hop to take away?
faq.a: Backwards, towards the smaller numbers. Adding hops forward, and taking away hops back.
asks: Do I hop forward or back?

faq.q: How do I keep track of the hops?
faq.a: Hold up one finger for each hop, or say them out loud. Stop when you have done the right number of hops.
asks: How do I count my hops back?

faq.a: Take away means some things are removed, so you have fewer. Twelve sweets take away five eaten leaves seven.

faq.q: Can I use a real line on the floor?
faq.a: Yes! Draw a line with chalk outside and jump backwards, or use a ruler. A teacher or grown-up can make a big floor number line with you.
asks: Tell me about the number line

facts: On a number line, adding moves forward and taking away moves back.

quiz.why: Start at ten and hop back three: nine, eight, seven.

wrong.1: Thirteen is ten add three. Taking away hops back.
wrong.2: Six is four hops back from ten. You only need three.

quiz.say: To take away on a number line, which way do you hop?
quiz.why: Taking away hops back, towards smaller numbers.

wrong.2: A number line goes back and forward, not up.
